Types are the vehicle’s powertrain. Unknown means the powertrain could not be determined, not that the tyre size is unknown — every vehicle in this donut is missing tyre sizes.

What kind of vehicle is missing tyre sizes, over time

Every vehicle in this chart is already missing tyre sizes. The lines show what those vehicles were — the make-up of the gap, month by month. Unknown powertrain means the vehicle’s own type could not be determined: no engine string in the log and no match in the EV catalogue, almost all of them AU_SCA iframe records with every spec field null.

Three reasons a vehicle has nothing to fit

The 249,968 unfitted vehicles split into three problems, each with a different owner and a different fix.

146,865

Spec is known, sizes are missing

The vehicle matches a row in the fitment table but no tyre sizes are recorded against it. Catalogue work.

98,597

Spec never matched

Make, model and series do not resolve to any row in the fitment table. Mapping and naming work.

4,506

Vehicle never identified

No make was captured, so nothing can be looked up. Capture work in the lookup flow.

Vehicle log report

25,000 vehicles with two or more requests, ordered by request count from largest to smallest, and by most recent request where counts are equal. Includes make, model, year, engine, EV class, tyre fitment and sizes.

Read these before acting on the counts

Each was found while building the underlying report. None is blocking, all are worth an owner.

Fitted means listed

A vehicle counts as fitted when its make, model and series resolve to a fitment row that has tyre sizes against it. That says the sizes exist in the catalogue, not that the customer was shown them. tyre_options is empty on every mirrored row, so the log cannot confirm what was actually served.

Empty tyre options

tyre_options is the literal string [] on all 324,350 mirrored rows. 1,140 rows carry a real tyre_options_added_at timestamp anyway, which says the field was populated upstream and lost in the mirror.

Vehicles with no make

4,506 vehicles carry 29,540 requests, averaging 6.6 each against about 1.0 everywhere else. Every spec field is null, so they can be neither classified nor fitment-checked. They come from the AU_SCA iframe integration.

Models never captured

Five makes reach the top thirty with no model recorded at all, worth 8,509 unfitted vehicles between them. Tesla and Ford stopped writing these in mid-2024, but Toyota and Nissan are still producing them in 2026.

Model names fragment

Counts group on the raw model string, so variants split into separate lines. Ford Falcon holds 4,161 vehicles under FALCON and 8 more under seven spellings including two of “FALCON GL,S-PAK” differing by one space. Small here, larger where a model splits evenly.

Unstable vehicle id

The fitment table’s vehicle_id is documented as session-ephemeral. Of 50,811 ids that match the log, 99.6% agree on make and model but the year rarely does, so the id resolves to the wrong variant. All joins here use make, model and series instead.

Stale fitment snapshot

The fitment table is a single snapshot dated 16 Jun 2026, three months behind the log. Vehicles first seen after that date can count as unmatched for no other reason.

Built from popeye_mirror.vehicle_log, RTB.vehicle_catalog_ev_ready and tyroola_reporting_prod.vehicle_tyre_fitment in heroic-ruler-198603. One row per vehicle_id, with requests summed across all stores. Fitment status is resolved on make, model and series, then counted at model level. Figures cover the full log, not the Req ≥ 2 subset in the spreadsheet.
